rounds.fact: Yelp started in 2004 as an email-based referral service before pivoting to the review-website format it's known for today, after users kept asking for a public place to post reviews.
Tom's Hardware built its reputation on exhaustive PC component benchmarks, becoming one of the go-to sites for hardware enthusiasts well before mainstream tech blogs existed.
Webshots was one of the most popular photo-sharing communities of the early 2000s, and was also widely used as a source for desktop wallpaper downloads.
Gizmodo's early scoops on unreleased Apple products, sometimes from leaked prototypes, made it one of the most closely watched (and occasionally legally threatened) tech blogs of the 2000s.
Newgrounds became the central hub for Flash animation and games in the early 2000s, launching the careers of several animators years before YouTube existed.
